label: Minimum-work vessel radius gives Murray's law r³ ∝ Q and the cubic junction rule
assumptions: Minimum effort read as Murray's (1926) cost per unit length: Poiseuille pumping power k Q²/r⁴ plus a blood-volume cost m r², k, m, Q, r > 0; every vessel at a junction minimizes its own cost with shared k and m, and flow is conserved (Q₀ = Q₁ + Q₂). General form: cost k Q^a/r^b + m r^c with a, b, c > 0. Friction family: Darcy–Weisbach power with friction factor ∝ Re^(-β), Re ∝ Q/r, β < 3.
scope_note: Proves the stationary radius is the strict global minimizer, r³ = √(2k/m)·Q, r₀³ = r₁³ + r₂³, and in general r₀^α = r₁^α + r₂^α with α = (b+c)/a (5/2 for a wall-surface cost). Corrects the approach: (b+2)/a = 7/3 holds on the whole line 3b + 6 = 7a, so (a, b) is not unique; it is unique, (3, 5) at β = 0, only within the friction-law family. Covers the radius consequence of Thompson's minimum-effort principle, not branching angles; whether real vessels obey it is left to data.

label: Structures that must resist bending are built as hollow tubes
reason: Concerns tubular construction for bending stiffness, not vascular flow; its mathematical core is formalized in ThompsonLaws.HollowTube (reports/HollowTube.json), not in this module.
